title: Flip Flap Dribbling Feint
content: The flip flap, also known as the elástico or snakebite, is a close-control dribbling technique designed to deceive an opponent by creating a false directional cue. The player initiates the move by pushing the ball outward with the outside of their dominant foot, then rapidly swings the same foot around the ball to push it sharply to the non-dominant side. This sudden change in direction, combined with the footwork, tricks the defender into committing to the wrong side. Success relies not just on footwork precision but on explosive acceleration from a stationary or slow-moving position to exploit the space created by the defender’s misstep. It is most effective when the attacker has time to set up the move and the defender is close enough to be deceived but not so close that the ball is easily stolen. The move is particularly useful in tight spaces where a quick change of direction can bypass a one-on-one challenge.
